newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CZECHS FIGHT BACK TO WIN 2-1.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CZECHS FIGHT BACK TO WIN 2-1.

text.p: Titleholders the Czech Republic came from behind to beat Germany 2-1 in their opening game in the ice hockey world championship on Saturday.
Vladimir Vujtek set up two goals in the last 15 minutes to save the day for the Czechs, who had failed to outsmart German goalkeeper Joseph Heiss in the first two periods.
Germany took the lead on a power play goal in the second period, defenceman Mirko Ludemann scoring with just eight seconds left of Ladislv Benysek's two-minute penalty for holding.
In the third period, the Czechs strung together the kind of passes that had eluded them in the opening 40 minutes, though they were still but a shadow of the side who won gold in Vienna last year.
"We knew it would be difficult to play Germany, but it became even more diffcult than we had expected," Czech coach Slavomir Lener said.
"The worst was that we were not able to score a single power-play goal," he said. The Germans had five two-minute penalties.
Martin Prochazka found the net in the 46th minute, slamming the puck home at the far post from a pass by Vujtek. The tired German defence were in tatters.
With less than five minutes to play, Vujtek and Roman Simicek broke through the German rearguard and Simicek scored the winner virtually unchallenged.
